# Read in Data

```{r}
# Clearing environment so code runs fresh
  rm(list=ls())

#versions of surveys have slightly different column formats (e.g., HRV questionnaire only asked after covid restrictions were lifted; presence of in person vs remote variable; position of BDI)

# Read in lifted COVID restrictions subjective questionnaire (i.e., in-person with Zoom or fully remote session choice)
  #variable "in person" where 1 is in person with Zoom and 2 remote
  #need to add this variable to original and COVID-restricted questionnaires so can differentiate formats once merged, and make sure a 3rd code for fully in person is added
choice_survey <- read.csv(here("Subjective Data", "Frienpathy Questionnaire-Full - Revised Fall 2021_Mixed Format.csv"))

# Read in original subjective questionnaire (i.e., in-person study sessions)
inperson_survey <- read.csv(here("Subjective Data", "Original Frienpathy Questionnaire_In-person.csv"))
  
# Read in COVID-restricted subjective questionnaire (i.e., remote study sessions)
remote_survey <- read.csv(here("Subjective Data", "Frienpathy Questionnaire-Full - Revised Fall 2020_Remote.csv"))

#Read in PANAS from listeners' post-problem conversations
PANAS_postprob <- read.csv(here("Subjective Data", "Co-rumination Listener-Frienpathy_October 8, 2025_16.21.csv"))
  #determined that this contains listeners' PANAS post problem conversations by looking at SID 2062a's progression through all surveys; sequential completion was: Neutral.csv, problem.csv, post-rum.csv, co-rum listener.csv (for friend B first), co-rum talker (for friend A second)

#Read in PANAS from listeners' post-neutral conversations
PANAS_postneut <- read.csv(here("Subjective Data/Frienpathy_ Neutral Interaction_October 8, 2025_16.44.csv"))
  #SIDs 2001a-2021b missing, so exploratory analysis of post-neutral convo & post-problem convo diff score will use reduced sample


```


## Add in person variable to original and covid-restricted surveys

```{r}

#Add in person variable to original survey
#coding as 3 to signify fully in person format (rather than in person with Zoom as in choice_survey)
inperson_survey <- inperson_survey %>%
  mutate(In.Person. = 3)

#add in person variable to covid-restricted survey
#2 = fully remote
remote_survey <- remote_survey %>%
  mutate(In.Person. = 2)

#Ensure in person variable is numeric for all surveys
is.numeric(choice_survey$In.Person.) # 1 = in person with zoom  
is.numeric(inperson_survey$In.Person.)
is.numeric(remote_survey$In.Person.)

choice_survey$In.Person. <- as.numeric(choice_survey$In.Person.)
is.numeric(choice_survey$In.Person.)

```

##Wrangle columns of interest and arrange

```{r}

#rename variables to be called SID 
inperson_survey <- inperson_survey %>%
  rename(SID = RecipientFirstName)

remote_survey <- remote_survey %>%
  rename(SID = Q1517)

choice_survey <- choice_survey %>%
  rename(SID = Q1517)

#remove Qualtrics metadata rows from SID columns
inperson_survey <- inperson_survey[-c(1:7), ]

remote_survey <- remote_survey[-c(1:2), ]

choice_survey <- choice_survey[-c(1:2), ]

PANAS_postprob <- PANAS_postprob[-c(1:6), ] #also remove rows w/ no SID data

PANAS_postneut <- PANAS_postneut[-c(1:3), ]

#check which participants' partners not present in data by creating new variable to note this
  #create new variable that isolates digit portion of SIDs, i.e., indicates shared dyad ID
  #for new variable, convert numeric SIDs to character because substr() works on text strings, not numbers
inperson_survey$dyadID <- substr(as.character(inperson_survey$SID), 1, nchar(as.character(inperson_survey$SID)) - 1) #-1 removes letters from SIDs

remote_survey$dyadID <- substr(as.character(remote_survey$SID), 1, nchar(as.character(remote_survey$SID)) - 1) #-1 removes letters from SIDs

choice_survey$dyadID <- substr(as.character(choice_survey$SID), 1, nchar(as.character(choice_survey$SID)) - 1) #-1 removes letters from SIDs

PANAS_postprob$dyadID <- substr(as.character(PANAS_postprob$SID), 1, nchar(as.character(PANAS_postprob$SID)) - 1) #-1 removes letters from SIDs

PANAS_postneut$dyadID <- substr(as.character(PANAS_postneut$SID), 1, nchar(as.character(PANAS_postneut$SID)) - 1) #-1 removes letters from SIDs

inperson_survey <- inperson_survey %>% #2022a, 2023a, and 2027a missing partners
  group_by(dyadID) %>%
  mutate(has_partner = n() == 2) %>%
  ungroup()

remote_survey <- remote_survey %>% #there are 2 2057b participants when there should only be one; I think that this was a typo and that the second 2057b ptp (row 43) should actually be 2058b because when you look at the qualtrics metadata for start and end date at the beginning of the data frame, this ptp and 2058a start and end the questionnaire at similar times (just as the first instance of 2057b and 2057a do); therefore, renaming this ptp 2058b
  group_by(dyadID) %>%
  mutate(has_partner = n() == 2) %>%
  ungroup()

#rename duplicate 2057b SID to 2058b
#first make sure R knows how to differentiate duplicates
remote_survey$SID <- make.unique(as.character(remote_survey$SID))
remote_survey$SID <- recode(remote_survey$SID, "2057b.1" = "2058b")   

#confirm remote_survey no longer missing partner data
remote_survey$dyadID <- substr(as.character(remote_survey$SID), 1, nchar(as.character(remote_survey$SID)) - 1)  

remote_survey <- remote_survey %>%
  group_by(dyadID) %>%
  mutate(has_partner = n() == 2) %>%
  ungroup() #confirmed


choice_survey <- choice_survey %>% #2089b (row 59) has duplicate data—looks like 2nd instance should be discarded b/c many missing values and survey unfinished compared to first instance; same issue for 2096b (row 68); remove these duplicates 
  group_by(dyadID) %>%
  mutate(has_partner = n() == 2) %>%
  ungroup()

#remove 2089b and 2096b duplicates
choice_survey$SID <- make.unique(as.character(choice_survey$SID))

choice_survey <- choice_survey[-c(59, 68), ]

#rename 2096b.1 SID to 2096b
choice_survey$SID <- recode(choice_survey$SID, "2096b.1" = "2096b")   

#confirm choice_survey no longer has duplicate partner data
choice_survey$dyadID <- substr(as.character(choice_survey$SID), 1, nchar(as.character(choice_survey$SID)) - 1)  

choice_survey <- choice_survey %>%
  group_by(dyadID) %>%
  mutate(has_partner = n() == 2) %>%
  ungroup() #confirmed

PANAS_postprob <- PANAS_postprob %>%  #3 instances of 2042 and 2040 and 2043 data
  group_by(dyadID) %>%
  mutate(has_partner = n() == 2) %>%
  ungroup() 

#removing third instances of 2042 and 2040 and 2043 data which do not contain values
PANAS_postprob$SID <- make.unique(as.character(PANAS_postprob$SID))

PANAS_postprob <- PANAS_postprob[-c(84, 85, 92), ]

PANAS_postprob <- PANAS_postprob %>%   
  group_by(dyadID) %>%
  mutate(has_partner = n() == 2) %>%
  ungroup() #confirmed

PANAS_postneut <- PANAS_postneut %>% #2052 missing partner; 3 instances of 2057
  group_by(dyadID) %>%
  mutate(has_partner = n() == 2) %>%
  ungroup() 

#removing third instance of 2057 which does not contain values
PANAS_postneut$SID <- make.unique(as.character(PANAS_postneut$SID))

PANAS_postneut <- PANAS_postneut[-c(74), ]

#make sure survey versions share column names of interest

#in-person survey has variable labels Q832-Q851 for PANAS items; relabel to match other surveys
inperson_survey <- inperson_survey %>%
  rename(PANAS.1 = Q832, PANAS.2 = Q833, PANAS.3 = Q834, PANAS.4 = Q835, PANAS.5 = Q836,
         PANAS.6 = Q837, PANAS.7 = Q838, PANAS.8 = Q839, PANAS.9 = Q840, PANAS.10 = Q841,
         PANAS.11 = Q842, PANAS.12 = Q843, PANAS.13 = Q844, PANAS.14 = Q845, PANAS.15 = Q846,
         PANAS.16 = Q847, PANAS.17 = Q848, PANAS.18 = Q849, PANAS.19 = Q850, PANAS.20 = Q851)

#sample size before participant removal

print(length(unique(inperson_survey$SID))) #n = 45 (21 dyads + 2022a, 2023a, and 2027a missing partners)
                      
print(length(unique(remote_survey$SID))) #n = 50 (25 dyads)             
                      
print(length(unique(choice_survey$SID))) #n = 80 (40 dyads)

#total individuals across surveys = 175
#total dyads across surveys = 86

#remove participants from data due to research team decisions  

#remove 2045a & 2045b: they misunderstood the task
#remove 2051a & 2051b: couldn't complete study in private space
remote_survey <- remote_survey[-c(17, 18, 29, 30), ]

#remove 2067a & 2067b: couldn't complete study in private space
#remove 2096a: recording inaudible so can't use their data  
#remove 2097b: recording inaudible so can't use their data  
choice_survey <- choice_survey[-c(11, 12, 69, 72), ]

PANAS_postprob <- PANAS_postprob[-c(88, 89, 100, 101, 132, 133, 191, 192), ]

#make all SIDs only include lowercase values and ensure no white space
choice_survey <- choice_survey %>%
  mutate(SID = str_to_lower(SID),     # lowercase
         SID = str_trim(SID))         # remove leading/trailing whitespace

remote_survey <- remote_survey %>%
  mutate(SID = str_to_lower(SID),      
         SID = str_trim(SID))

inperson_survey <- inperson_survey %>%
  mutate(SID = str_to_lower(SID),     
         SID = str_trim(SID))

PANAS_postprob <- PANAS_postprob %>%
  mutate(SID = str_to_lower(SID),     
         SID = str_trim(SID))

#select columns of interest from each survey before merge

##inperson_survey: remove columns not of interest  
inperson_survey <- inperson_survey[ , -c(1:10, 12:18, 20, 26:158, 190:221, 246:464, 465:484, 485:522, 524:525)]

##remote_survey: remove columns not of interest  
remote_survey <- remote_survey[ , -c(1:17, 19, 21, 27:159, 191:222, 247:591, 592:611, 612:649, 651:652)]

##choice_survey: remove columns not of interest  
choice_survey <- choice_survey[ , -c(1:17, 19, 21, 28:184, 216:247, 272:616, 617:636, 637:676)]

##PANAS post prob convo: remove columns not of interest  
PANAS_postprob <- PANAS_postprob[ , -c(1, 39:66)] 

##PANAS post neutral convo: remove columns not of interest  
PANAS_postneut <- PANAS_postneut[ , -c(1:17, 39:40)]  

#rename demographics columns
inperson_survey <- inperson_survey %>%
  rename(Age = Q1, Gender = Q2, GenderText = Q2_.999_TEXT, Ethnicity = Q3, Race = Q4, RaceText = Q4_6_TEXT)

remote_survey <- remote_survey %>%
  rename(Age = Q1, Gender = Q2, GenderText = Q2_.999_TEXT, Ethnicity = Q3, Race = Q4, RaceText = Q4_6_TEXT)

choice_survey <- choice_survey %>%

#order rows alpha-numerically by SID
inperson_survey <- inperson_survey %>%
  mutate(
    SID_num = as.numeric(str_extract(SID, "^\\d+")), #focuses on numeric part of SID
    SID_letter = str_extract(SID, "[a-zA-Z]+$") #focuses on letter part of SID
  ) %>%

remote_survey <- remote_survey %>%

    SID_letter = str_extract(SID, "[a-zA-Z]+$") #focuses on letter part of SID
  ) %>%

  ) %>%

PANAS_postneut <- PANAS_postneut %>%
```

## Merge survey data frames

```{r}

#merge surveys
combined_survey <- bind_rows(
  inperson_survey,
  remote_survey,
  choice_survey
)

#merge post prob convo PANAS items with combined survey 
combined_survey <- combined_survey %>%
  left_join(PANAS_postprob, by = "SID")  #keep participants with missing PANAS scores

combined_survey <- combined_survey[ , -c(64:79)]  

#merge post neutral convo PANAS items with combined survey for exploratory purposes only
neut_baseline_combined_survey <- combined_survey %>%
  left_join(PANAS_postneut, by = "SID")

```

```{r}
#new data frame combining demographic variables 
  #examined JW's dissertation ch to understand gender and race distributions, concluding that b/c 69.3% identified as women, 28.2% as men, and 2.5% as other, responses coded as -1 should represent women since most frequent; 1 = men; -999 = other
  #Q2: gender; Q3: ethnicity (1 = Hispanic or Latino; 2 = not); Q4: race (1 = American Indian/Alaskan Native, 2 = Asian, 3 = Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander, 4 = Black or African American, 5 = White, 6 = Other)

table(choice_survey$Q2)
table(choice_survey$Q4)

cols_desired <- c("SID", "Age", "Gender", "GenderText", "Ethnicity", "Race", "RaceText", "In.Person.")

  choice_survey[cols_desired],
  remote_survey[cols_desired],

# #rename demographic columns in new data frame

  mutate(
    Gender = recode(Gender, "-1" = "Female", "1" = "Male", "-999" = "Other"),
    Ethnicity = recode(Ethnicity, "1" = "Hispanic or Latino", "2" = "Not Hispanic or Latino"),
    Race = recode(Race, "1" = "American Indian/Alaskan Native", "2" = "Asian", "3" = "Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander", "4" = "Black or African American", "5" = "White", "6" = "Other", "1,5" = "American Indian/Alaskan Native and White",  
                       "2,5" = "Asian and White", "4,5" = "Black or African American and White", "5,6" = "White and Other"),
    In.Person. = recode(In.Person., "1" = "In-person with Zoom", "2" = "Remote", "3" = "Fully in-person"))

#order rows alpha-numerically by SID

  mutate(

    SID_letter = str_extract(SID, "[a-zA-Z]+$") #focuses on letter part of SID
  ) %>%
```

#Understand what SIDs are shared vs. not across data types: subjective, neural, HR, behavioral
``` {r}

# Subjective data
combinedsurv_SIDs <- as.character(combined_survey$SID)

# EEG files: get SIDs from file names
eeg_files <- list.files("/Volumes/gutsell-lab-1/Sharde_Building on Friempathy/EEG Data/friempathy_EEG_analysis_scripts/friempathydata", full.names = FALSE, recursive = FALSE) #may need to repaste path from server; SIDs are folders not csv files so this is why using recursive
eeg_SIDs <- str_extract(eeg_files, "^[0-9]+[ab]?") # extracts IDs  

#dir.exists("/Volumes/gutsell-lab/Sharde_Building on Friempathy/EEG Data/friempathy_EEG_analysis_scripts/friempathydata")

# HRV files: get SIDs from file names
hrv_files <- list.files("/Volumes/gutsell-lab-1/Sharde_Building on Friempathy/HR Analyses/HR Data", pattern = "\\.csv.zip$", full.names = FALSE)
hrv_SIDs <- str_extract(hrv_files, "^[0-9]+[aAbB]?")

hrv_SIDs <- tolower(hrv_SIDs)

# Read in composite behavioral codes

#behav_data <- 

#unique SIDs
combinedsurv_id <- unique(combinedsurv_SIDs)
eeg_id <- unique(eeg_SIDs)
hr_id <- unique(hrv_SIDs)
#behav_id <- unique(behav_SIDs)


#see IDs shared vs not in a table
SID_list <- unique(c(combinedsurv_id, eeg_id, hr_id)) #behav_id

comparison <- data.frame(
  SID = SID_list,
  in_combinedsurv = SID_list %in% combinedsurv_id,
  in_EEG = SID_list %in% eeg_id,
  in_HRV = SID_list %in% hr_id)
  #in_behav = all_SIDs %in% behav_id)

comparison$SID <- as.character(comparison$SID)

comparison

comparison <- comparison %>%
  arrange(
    as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9]", "", SID)),  # numeric part for ordering
    SID)                                   # keeps 'a'/'b' suffix order 


#summarize how many SIDs present per data type

# Select only logical columns (i.e., data type columns)
logical_cols <- comparison %>% select(-SID)

# Count TRUE per column
totalSIDs <- colSums(logical_cols) #n for combined is 166 not 167 for some reason
totalSIDs

#summarize which SIDs missing per data type
missingSIDs <- lapply(logical_cols, function(x) comparison$SID[!x])
missingSIDs

length(missingSIDs$in_combinedsurv)
length(missingSIDs$in_EEG)
length(missingSIDs$in_HRV)

#summarize SIDs shared across all data formats, as these individuals will be primary analysis (could conduct exploratory analysis for baseline faa-task based faa with eeg data nonwithstanding subjective data if Jenny approves since larger N)
sharedSIDs_all <- comparison$SID[
  comparison$in_combinedsurv &
  comparison$in_EEG &
  comparison$in_HRV
]

length(sharedSIDs_all) # n = 70

#shared across subjective and eeg
sharedSIDs_surveeg <- comparison$SID[
  comparison$in_combinedsurv &
```
